title: NASA opens registration to send names to Titan on Dragonfly mission
excerpt: The public can submit names to be carried on a microchip aboard the rotorcraft until January 15, 2027.
bodyHtml:
NASA announced on October 29, 2026, that the public can submit their names to be included on a microchip aboard the Dragonfly rotorcraft. The mission is scheduled to launch in 2028 and arrive at Saturn’s moon Titan in 2034.

Participants can register their names and receive a digital boarding pass through the NASA website. The Dragonfly rotorcraft is currently being assembled at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory in Laurel, Maryland.

Dragonfly is the fourth mission in NASA’s New Frontiers Program, managed by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama. The rotorcraft will explore Titan, a world with a thick atmosphere, rivers and lakes of liquid methane, and a landscape rich in organic material.

The deadline to secure a place on the mission passenger list is 11:59 p.m. EST January 15, 2027.
